title: AIP: Subverting Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Adversarial Instructional Prompt
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces AIP, a black-box attack that crafts natural-looking adversarial instructional prompts (paired with poisoned documents and a stealthy trigger) to covertly steer RAG retrieval and generation toward attacker-targeted outputs while preserving clean-task utility.

title: Astute RAG: Overcoming Imperfect Retrieval Augmentation and Knowledge Conflicts for Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes ASTUTE RAG, a training-free method that elicits LLM internal knowledge, performs iterative source-aware consolidation with retrieved passages to resolve conflicts, and selects the final answer by reliability comparison; demonstrates worst-case robustness under imperfect retrieval.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression: Paper's primary focus is knowledge conflict resolution; it fits noisy retrieval too but is more centrally a knowledge_conflict/calibration paper.

title: BadRAG: Identifying Vulnerabilities in Retrieval Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: BadRAG crafts adversarial passages via contrastive optimization that are retrieved only for trigger queries, enabling DoS and sentiment-steering attacks on RAG-based LLMs with minimal poisoning ratio.

title: Reliable Decision-Making via Calibration-Oriented Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes CalibRAG, which trains a forecasting function over (temperature, query, document) to predict decision correctness, enabling reranking and calibrated confidence for RAG-supported decision-making.

title: Certifiably Robust RAG against Retrieval Corruption
brief_actual_contribution: RobustRAG introduces an isolate-then-aggregate defense (keyword and decoding aggregation) providing certifiable robustness guarantees against bounded retrieval corruption attacks in RAG.

title: Chain-of-Note: Enhancing Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces Chain-of-Note, which has RALMs generate per-document reading notes to assess relevance, leverage intrinsic knowledge, and abstain ('unknown') when evidence is insufficient, improving noise and unknown robustness across open-domain QA benchmarks.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: CRAG introduces a lightweight T5-based retrieval evaluator that scores retrieved documents and triggers Correct/Incorrect/Ambiguous actions—refining internal knowledge or invoking web search—to improve RAG robustness when retrieval is poor.

title: CtrlA: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Inherent Control
brief_actual_contribution: CtrlA extracts honesty and confidence direction features from LLM representations to steer outputs and monitor confidence, triggering retrieval adaptively when the model is unconfident.

title: FaithfulRAG: Fact-Level Conflict Modeling for Context-Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: FaithfulRAG resolves parametric vs. retrieved knowledge conflicts by mining self-facts, aligning them with retrieved context chunks, and running a self-think module to reconcile discrepancies before generation.

title: Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Context
brief_actual_contribution: Shows RALMs are brittle to irrelevant retrieved context and proposes two mitigations: NLI-based filtering of non-entailing passages and fine-tuning on mixed relevant/irrelevant contexts to teach robust use of retrieval in single- and multi-hop QA.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces the original Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework combining a DPR retriever with a BART generator, fine-tuned end-to-end for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks.

title: Phantom: General Backdoor Attacks on Retrieval Augmented Language Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Phantom is a backdoor poisoning attack on RAG that uses a two-stage optimization (HotFlip on retriever + Multi-Coordinate Gradient on generator) to craft a single poisoned document retrieved only when a natural trigger appears in the query, enabling refusal, biased opinion, harmful behavior, passage exfiltration, and tool misuse across open and closed LLMs including a black-box attack on NVIDIA ChatRTX.

title: PoisonedRAG: Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces PoisonedRAG, the first knowledge-corruption attack on RAG, formulating malicious-text crafting as an optimization with retrieval and generation conditions, achieving high ASRs in black-box and white-box settings across datasets and LLMs.

title: Poisoning Retrieval Corpora by Injecting Adversarial Passages
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a HotFlip-based corpus poisoning attack that crafts a small number of adversarial passages to be retrieved by dense retrievers for broad and out-of-domain query distributions, exposing vulnerabilities in Contriever, DPR, ANCE, and ColBERT.

title: Investigating the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation at the Query Level
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a framework and empirical study (1092+ experiments) showing that minor query perturbations (typos, redundancy, formality, ambiguity) significantly affect retriever, generator, and end-to-end RAG performance, with module-level decoupling analysis.

title: Enhancing Noise Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Adaptive Adversarial Training
brief_actual_contribution: Categorizes retrieval noise into relevant, irrelevant, and counterfactual types, proposes RAAT (adaptive adversarial training with noise-aware multi-task learning), and introduces RAG-Bench for evaluating noise robustness on three open-domain QA datasets.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
brief_actual_contribution: A comprehensive survey of RAG architectures (retriever/generator/hybrid/robustness), enhancements, evaluation frameworks, and benchmarks, with comparative performance analyses.

title: Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey
brief_actual_contribution: A survey of RAG evaluation that organizes benchmarks, metrics, and datasets through a unified framework (Auepora) covering retrieval and generation targets.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
brief_actual_contribution: A comprehensive survey of RAG for LLMs covering architectures (Naive/Advanced/Modular RAG), retrieval/generation/augmentation components, evaluation, and future directions.

title: RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: RAGTruth is a ~18K-response corpus with word-level hallucination annotations across QA, data-to-text, and summarization in RAG settings, used to benchmark hallucination detection methods and fine-tune detectors.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces RGB, a bilingual benchmark evaluating LLM RAG along four abilities: noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness.

title: URAG: A Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces URAG, a benchmark that reformulates open-ended RAG tasks into MCQA and applies conformal prediction to jointly evaluate accuracy and uncertainty of 8 RAG methods across 5 domains, including under irrelevant/noisy retrieval.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression: Primary focus is uncertainty quantification benchmark; noisy retrieval is one experimental dimension

title: Trust or Abstain? A Self-Aware RAG Approach
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes SABER, a frozen-LLM probe combining self-prior and source-conditional reasoning representations to estimate PK/CK reliability and drive a 4-cell trust/abstain decision; also builds a ground-truth-aligned knowledge-conflict benchmark with faithfulness metrics.

title: The First Drop of Ink: Nonlinear Impact of Misleading Information in Long-Context Reasoning
brief_actual_contribution: Identifies a nonlinear 'first drop of ink' effect where a small fraction of hard distractors in long contexts disproportionately degrades QA accuracy, with theoretical analysis via attention/softmax mechanics and validation on retrieval heads.

title: ProGRank: Probe-Gradient Reranking to Defend Dense-Retriever RAG from Corpus Poisoning
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes ProGRank, a training-free retriever-side reranking defense that uses probe-gradient instability signals under randomized perturbations to demote poisoned passages in dense-retriever RAG.

title: Overcoming the Retrieval Barrier: Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild for LLM Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a black-box CEM-based prefix optimization to guarantee retrieval of injected malicious documents (trigger fragment + attack fragment), enabling end-to-end indirect prompt injection attacks against RAG and agentic systems, evaluated across 11 BEIR benchmarks and 8 embedding models.

title: Over-Searching in Search-Augmented Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Defines and systematically evaluates over-searching in search-augmented LLMs, introduces the Tokens Per Correctness (TPC) metric, and releases the OverSearchQA benchmark for abstention/efficiency evaluation.

title: NAACL: Noise-AwAre Verbal Confidence Calibration for Robust LLMs in RAG Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes NAACL, an SFT framework with noise-aware rules (conflict independence, noise invariance, parametric fallback) that calibrates verbal confidence of LLMs in RAG under irrelevant/counterfactual retrieval, improving ECE substantially.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Primary contribution is calibration; noisy retrieval is the diagnostic lens, so inclusion is justified but secondary.

title: CoRect: Context-Aware Logit Contrast for Hidden State Rectification to Resolve Knowledge Conflicts
brief_actual_contribution: CoRect is a training-free, target-agnostic method that uses context-aware logit contrast to localize FFN layers exhibiting 'parametric suppression' and rectifies their hidden states to resolve knowledge conflicts in RAG, improving QA and summarization faithfulness.

title: CleanBase: Detecting Malicious Documents in RAG Knowledge Databases
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes CleanBase, a defense that detects malicious documents in a RAG knowledge database by constructing a similarity graph and identifying cliques of semantically similar injected documents, with theoretical FPR/FNR bounds.

title: AdversarialCoT: Single-Document Retrieval Poisoning for LLM Reasoning
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces AdversarialCoT, a query-specific single-document poisoning attack that iteratively crafts adversarial chain-of-thought documents to mislead retrieval-augmented LLM reasoning under a black-box setting.

title: Addressing Corpus Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on RAG Using Sparse Attention
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Sparse Document Attention RAG (SDAG), a block-sparse attention defense at inference time that disables cross-document attention to mitigate corpus poisoning attacks, outperforming SOTA defenses.

title: Why Uncertainty Estimation Methods Fall Short in RAG: An Axiomatic Analysis
brief_actual_contribution: Analyzes failure modes of uncertainty estimation methods in RAG setups, defines five axioms an effective UE method should satisfy with retrieved context, and derives a calibration function that improves AUROC.

title: TrustRAG: Enhancing Robustness and Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: TrustRAG is a two-stage defense framework against RAG corpus poisoning that uses K-means clustering with ROUGE-based filtering to remove tightly-clustered malicious documents, then resolves conflicts between internal LLM knowledge and external retrieved evidence via self-assessment.
issues: Knowledge conflict and contextual faithfulness: Primarily an adversarial-corruption defense, but it explicitly addresses knowledge conflict resolution as a core mechanism.

title: Traceback of Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes RAGForensics, a traceback system that iteratively retrieves and LLM-classifies poisoned texts in RAG knowledge bases responsible for incorrect outputs, evaluated against PoisonedRAG and instruction injection attacks plus adaptive variants.

title: Through the Stealth Lens: Attention-Aware Defenses Against Poisoning in RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Formalizes a stealth distinguishability game for RAG poisoning and proposes an attention-variance filter (AV Filter) using NPAS to detect and remove poisoned passages, plus adaptive attacks to evade it.

title: Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation against Poisoning Attacks
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes RAGuard, a defense against RAG knowledge-base poisoning that combines retrieval expansion with chunk-wise perplexity and text similarity filtering to detect and remove poisoned texts.

title: SeCon-RAG: A Two-Stage Semantic Filtering and Conflict-Free Framework for Trustworthy RAG
brief_actual_contribution: SeCon-RAG defends against corpus poisoning via a two-stage pipeline combining clustering+semantic-graph filtering (via an Entity-Intent-Relation Extractor) and a conflict-aware filtering module that resolves contradictions between query, retrieved documents, and the LLM's internal knowledge.

title: Safeguarding RAG Pipelines with GMTP: A Gradient-based Masked Token Probability Method for Poisoned Document Detection
brief_actual_contribution: GMTP defends RAG against corpus poisoning by identifying high-gradient tokens, masking them, and using an MLM to detect anomalously low predicted probabilities indicative of injected adversarial tokens.

title: SafeRAG: Benchmarking Security in Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Model
brief_actual_contribution: SafeRAG is a Chinese benchmark for evaluating RAG security against four adversarial attack tasks (silver noise, inter-context conflict, soft ad, white DoS) injected at various pipeline stages.

title: Rescuing the Unpoisoned: Efficient Defense against Knowledge Corruption Attacks on RAG Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes RAGDefender, a lightweight post-retrieval defense that clusters and filters adversarial passages to mitigate knowledge corruption (poisoning) attacks on RAG systems.

title: ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes ReliabilityRAG, a defense against retrieval corruption (corpus poisoning, prompt injection) using a Maximum Independent Set over a contradiction graph that leverages document reliability/rank, with provable robustness guarantees and a scalable weighted sample-and-aggregate variant.

title: RAGPart \& RAGMask: Retrieval-Stage Defenses Against Corpus Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces two retrieval-stage defenses (RAGPart via fragment partitioning/averaging and RAGMask via token-masking similarity shifts) against corpus poisoning in RAG, plus an interpretable AdvRAGgen attack.

title: PoisonArena: Uncovering Competing Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces PoisonArena, a benchmark for evaluating competing poisoning attacks in RAG using a Bradley-Terry model, showing that strong single-attacker methods often fail under multi-attacker competition.

title: ParamMute: Suppressing Knowledge-Critical FFNs for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Identifies a subset of mid-to-deep FFN layers that drive unfaithful generation in RAG, proposes suppression + preference optimization (ParamMute) to enhance contextual faithfulness, and introduces the CoFaithfulQA benchmark for evaluating faithfulness under knowledge conflicts.

title: PR-Attack: Coordinated Prompt-RAG Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Large Language Models via Bilevel Optimization
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces PR-Attack, a bilevel-optimization-based coordinated poisoning attack on RAG-based LLMs that jointly optimizes a small number of poisoned documents and a backdoor trigger in the prompt to achieve stealthy, high-ASR attacks.

title: POISONCRAFT: Practical Poisoning of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes POISONCRAFT, a query-agnostic poisoning attack on RAG that injects optimized adversarial documents to make LLMs recommend a malicious URL, demonstrating effectiveness, transferability across retrievers, and robustness against defenses.

title: Magic Mushroom: A Customizable Benchmark for Fine-grained Analysis of Retrieval Noise Erosion in RAG Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces Magic Mushroom, a customizable QA benchmark with four fine-grained retrieval noise types (distracting, low-quality, inconsequential, irrelevant) for evaluating RAG robustness under configurable noise distributions.

title: MIRAGE: Misleading Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Black-box and Query-agnostic Poisoning Attacks
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes MIRAGE, a black-box, query-agnostic RAG corpus poisoning attack using persona-driven query synthesis, semantic anchoring, and adversarial test-time preference optimization, evaluated on a new long-form domain-specific benchmark.
issues: Adversarial corruption and security.: Assigned categories include evaluation_benchmark, which is also supported as the paper builds a dedicated long-form RAG poisoning benchmark, but the manuscript only cites it under adversarial corruption.

title: MAGIC: A Multi-Hop and Graph-Based Benchmark for Inter-Context Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces MAGIC, a knowledge-graph-based benchmark for evaluating inter-context knowledge conflict detection in RAG, featuring multi-hop and multi-conflict scenarios.

title: Do Retrieval Augmented Language Models Know When They Don't Know?
brief_actual_contribution: Investigates whether retrieval-augmented LLMs are well-calibrated and know when to refuse, finding that purely irrelevant retrieved contexts induce over-refusal and miscalibration; proposes uncertainty-based two-stage refusal mechanism.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Paper also strongly fits calibration_control and ood_uncertainty (assigned), and addresses noisy retrieval specifically through impact of irrelevant documents.

title: DRAGged into Conflicts: Detecting and Addressing Conflicting Sources in Search-Augmented LLMs
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a taxonomy of inter-context knowledge conflict types in RAG (no conflict, complementary, conflicting opinions, outdated, misinformation) and the CONFLICTS benchmark with expert annotations, showing LLMs struggle to adopt type-appropriate responses.

title: CUB: Benchmarking Context Utilisation Techniques for Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: CUB benchmarks seven context-utilisation manipulation techniques across 11 LMs on CounterFact, NQ, and DRUID under gold, conflicting, and irrelevant contexts, revealing trade-offs between faithfulness and robustness.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression: Paper covers knowledge conflict and distraction/irrelevant context evaluation; fits all assigned categories.

title: Benchmarking Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces RSB, a benchmark covering 13 poisoning attacks and 7 defenses against RAG across 15 QA datasets and multiple RAG architectures, with comprehensive empirical analysis.

title: Adaptive Retrieval Without Self-Knowledge? Bringing Uncertainty Back Home
brief_actual_contribution: Benchmarks 35 adaptive retrieval methods (8 recent pipelines + 27 uncertainty estimation methods) across 6 QA datasets with 10 metrics covering QA accuracy, efficiency (LLM/retrieval calls), and self-knowledge, showing UE methods match complex adaptive RAG pipelines at lower cost.

title: Glue pizza and eat rocks - Exploiting Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generative Models
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces LIAR, a bi-level optimization attack that crafts adversarial documents which are both preferentially retrieved and cause LLMs to produce harmful or enforced outputs, demonstrating RAG vulnerability in a gray-box setting.

title: WikiContradict: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Real-World Knowledge Conflicts from Wikipedia
brief_actual_contribution: Presents WikiContradict, a Wikipedia-based benchmark of 253 annotated instances with contradictory passages, used to evaluate how LLMs handle real-world inter-context knowledge conflicts in RAG settings.

title: Toward Robust RALMs: Revealing the Impact of Imperfect Retrieval on Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
assigned_categories: noisy_retrieval; distraction; knowledge_conflict; adversarial_corruption; ood_uncertainty; evaluation_benchmark
brief_actual_contribution: Systematically evaluates RALM robustness against unanswerable, adversarial, and conflicting retrieved documents, introducing GenADV adversarial passage generation and the RAD robustness metric for open-domain QA.

title: To Trust or Not to Trust? Enhancing Large Language Models' Situated Faithfulness to External Contexts
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces 'situated faithfulness' and benchmarks LLMs on QA with correct/incorrect contexts (including new RedditQA), proposing Self-Guided and Rule-Based Confidence Reasoning plus CR-DPO to calibrate trust between internal knowledge and external context.

title: Long-Context LLMs Meet RAG: Overcoming Challenges for Long Inputs in RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Empirically shows long-context RAG performance follows an inverted-U as retrieved passages increase due to hard negatives, and proposes retrieval reordering plus RAG-specific fine-tuning (implicit and reasoning-augmented) to improve robustness.

title: FaithEval: Can Your Language Model Stay Faithful to Context, Even If "The Moon is Made of Marshmallows"
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces FaithEval, a 4.9K-sample benchmark evaluating LLM contextual faithfulness under unanswerable, inconsistent, and counterfactual contexts, showing even SOTA models struggle to remain faithful to provided contexts.

title: Controlling Risk of Retrieval-augmented Generation: A Counterfactual Prompting Framework
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a counterfactual prompting framework to assess RAG predictive uncertainty by perturbing retrieval quality and usage, with a new benchmark and risk-aware metrics for abstention.

title: Context-DPO: Aligning Language Models for Context-Faithfulness
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces ConFiQA, a benchmark for evaluating context-faithfulness under knowledge conflicts in RAG, and Context-DPO, a DPO-based alignment method that improves LLMs' adherence to provided counterfactual context.

title: Why So Gullible? Enhancing the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Models against Counterfactual Noise
brief_actual_contribution: Shows that retrieval-augmented LMs (FiD, GPT-3.5) are brittle to counterfactual/conflicting documents, proposes a discriminator-based fine-tuning and prompting approach to improve robustness, and releases MACNOISE, an LLM-generated knowledge-conflict benchmark.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Paper is primarily about knowledge conflict / counterfactual noise rather than generic noisy retrieval or context compression, but conflict-induced noise reasonably fits the noisy retrieval category.

title: Learning to Filter Context for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: FILCO proposes sentence-level context filtering for RAG using STRINC, lexical overlap, and CXMI measures to remove distracting content from retrieved passages, training a filter model and showing gains across six knowledge-intensive tasks.

title: Investigating the Factual Knowledge Boundary of Large Language Models with Retrieval Augmentation
brief_actual_contribution: Empirical study of LLMs' perception of factual knowledge boundaries via priori/posteriori judgement, showing overconfidence, poor handling of internal-external knowledge conflicts, and improvements from retrieval augmentation, including a dynamic retrieval strategy based on self-judgement.

title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of Large Language Models in Knowledge Conflicts
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a framework to elicit parametric memory and construct coherent counter-memory, then analyzes LLM behavior in knowledge conflicts, finding high receptiveness to coherent counter-evidence but confirmation bias when memory-aligned evidence coexists.

title: CPA-RAG: Covert Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces CPA-RAG, a black-box covert poisoning attack on RAG that uses multi-LLM prompt-based generation and retriever-aware optimization to craft fluent adversarial passages that evade common defenses.

title: ] Typos that Broke the RAG's Back: Genetic Attack on RAG Pipeline by Simulating Documents in the Wild via Low-level Perturbations
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes GARAG, a black-box genetic algorithm that injects low-level typo perturbations into retrieved documents to jointly attack retriever and reader in RAG, showing significant performance degradation across QA datasets.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Paper is primarily an adversarial corruption attack; it also relates to noisy retrieval since perturbations simulate naturally noisy documents.

title: UniC-RAG: Universal Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes UniC-RAG, a universal knowledge corruption attack that jointly optimizes a small set of adversarial passages (via balanced similarity-based clustering and HotFlip) to compromise many diverse user queries in a RAG knowledge base, evaluating across datasets, retrievers, LLMs, and defenses.

title: Joint-GCG: Unified Gradient-Based Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Joint-GCG, a unified gradient-based corpus poisoning attack on RAG that jointly optimizes retriever and generator objectives via cross-vocabulary projection, gradient tokenization alignment, and adaptive weighted fusion.

title: GraphRAG under Fire
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces GRAGPOISON, a black-box poisoning attack tailored to GraphRAG that injects/enhances false relations to compromise multiple multi-hop queries simultaneously, and evaluates defenses.

title: Eyes-on-Me: Scalable RAG Poisoning through Transferable Attention-Steering Attractors
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes EYES-ON-ME, a modular RAG poisoning attack using reusable attention attractors that steer influential attention heads toward a focus region containing swappable payloads, achieving high attack success and transferability across retrievers/generators.

title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes AgentPoison, a backdoor attack on RAG-based LLM agents that optimizes triggers via constrained optimization to map triggered queries into a unique embedding region, ensuring high retrieval of malicious demonstrations and adversarial action generation.

title: ADMIT: Few-shot Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on RAG-based Fact Checking
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces ADMIT, a few-shot adversarial passage injection attack on RAG-based fact-checking systems that flips verification decisions across retrievers, LLMs, and domains under black-box access.

title: Worse than Zero-shot? A Fact-Checking Dataset for Evaluating the Robustness of RAG Against Misleading Retrievals
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces RAGUARD, a political fact-checking benchmark with Reddit-sourced documents labeled as supporting, misleading, or unrelated, showing that LLM RAG systems perform worse than zero-shot baselines under misleading retrievals.

title: TrustRAG: Enhancing Robustness and Trustworthiness in RAG
brief_actual_contribution: TrustRAG is a two-stage defense framework (K-means clustering + ROUGE filtering, then internal-knowledge conflict resolution) that mitigates single- and multi-document corpus poisoning attacks in RAG systems.

title: Practical Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: CorruptRAG is a practical single-text poisoning attack on RAG that uses adversarial templates (CorruptRAG-AS) and LLM-refined adversarial knowledge (CorruptRAG-AK) to manipulate generated answers, outperforming prior multi-text poisoning baselines and resisting four defenses.

title: Redefining Retrieval Evaluation in the Era of LLMs
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces UDCG, a utility- and distraction-aware retrieval evaluation metric that aligns IR scoring with LLM-consumer behavior, showing stronger correlation with end-to-end RAG accuracy than nDCG/MAP/MRR.

title: Epistemic Bias Injection: Biasing LLMs via Selective Context Retrieval
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes EBI, a stealthy RAG corpus poisoning attack that injects factually correct yet epistemically biased passages, introduces a polarization-score metric, builds an evaluation benchmark, and proposes BiasDef defense.

title: When Safety Becomes a Vulnerability: Exploiting LLM Alignment Homogeneity for Transferable Blocking in RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces TabooRAG, a black-box transferable blocking (denial-of-service) attack on RAG that exploits LLM safety alignment homogeneity by injecting restricted-risk-context documents to induce refusals.

title: DiscourseFlip: An Oblique Discourse-Level Opinion Manipulation Attack against Black-box Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a discourse-level opinion manipulation threat model against black-box RAG and proposes DiscourseFlip, a graph-guided agentic poisoning attack that propagates stance shifts across semantically related queries.

title: Confundo: Learning to Generate Robust Poison for Practical RAG Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Confundo, a fine-tuned LLM-based poison generator that produces robust, stealthy poison texts to attack practical RAG pipelines across multiple objectives (factual manipulation, opinion bias, hallucination).

title: BiRD: A Bidirectional Ranking Defense Mechanism for Retrieval Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes BiRD, a defense for RAG that filters poisoned documents by combining forward content relevance with backward ranking consistency, demonstrating reductions in attack success rate against PoisonedRAG and prompt-injection attacks.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes R2C, a consistency-based uncertainty quantification method for retrieval-augmented reasoning that perturbs reasoning paths via query paraphrasing, critical rethinking, and answer validation, improving AUROC and downstream abstention/model selection.

title: Parameters vs. Context: Fine-Grained Control of Knowledge Reliance in Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes CK-PLUG, a plug-and-play decoding-time method that detects parameter-context knowledge conflicts via a Confidence Gain (entropy) metric and modulates token distributions with a tunable parameter to control reliance on parametric vs. contextual knowledge in RAG.

title: Divide-Then-Align: Honest Alignment based on the Knowledge Boundary of RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Divide-Then-Align (DTA), a DPO-based post-training method that partitions RAG samples into four knowledge-boundary quadrants and teaches models to abstain ('I don't know') when queries fall outside both parametric and retrieval knowledge boundaries.

title: ATM: Adversarial Tuning Multi-agent System Makes a Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generator
brief_actual_contribution: ATM introduces an attacker-generator adversarial tuning loop where an attacker LLM injects fabricated/permuted documents to train a more robust RAG generator that resists noisy and fabricated retrieved content.

title: Understanding Data Poisoning Attacks for RAG: Insights and Algorithms
brief_actual_contribution: Analyzes targeted data poisoning attacks on RAG retrieval, showing effective attacks lie along low-variance directions, and proposes a DRS-based defense filter plus a DRS-regularized stealthier attack.

title: When Evidence Conflicts: Uncertainty and Order Effects in Retrieval-Augmented Biomedical Question Answering
brief_actual_contribution: Evaluates six open-weight LLMs on the HealthContradict biomedical QA benchmark under controlled correct/incorrect/conflicting-order evidence conditions, quantifying accuracy, calibration, and order-induced answer flips, and proposes a conflict-aware abstention score that outperforms confidence-only selective prediction.

title: The Synthetic Web: Adversarially-Curated Mini-Internets for Diagnosing Epistemic Weaknesses of Language Agents
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces Synthetic Web Benchmark, a procedurally generated environment for diagnosing how language agents fail under rank-controlled adversarial misinformation injection, with process traces and calibration metrics.

title: Seeing through the Conflict: Transparent Knowledge Conflict Handling in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes TCR, a plug-and-play RAG module that disentangles semantic relevance, factual consistency, and self-answerability into scalar signals fed via soft prompts to detect and resolve context-memory knowledge conflicts.

title: MEMSAD: Gradient-Coupled Anomaly Detection for Memory Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Agents
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes MEMSAD, a write-time anomaly detection defense against memory-poisoning attacks on retrieval-augmented LLM agents, with gradient-coupling theorems, certified detection radius, and minimax-optimal calibration guarantees.

title: LLM-Oriented Information Retrieval: A Denoising-First Perspective
brief_actual_contribution: A SIGIR'26 perspective/survey paper proposing denoising as the primary objective of LLM-oriented IR, with a pipeline-organized taxonomy spanning indexing, retrieval, context assembly, verification, and agentic loops, covering distractors, knowledge conflicts, and adversarial corruption.

title: Is Conformal Factuality for RAG-based LLMs Robust? Novel Metrics and Systematic Insights
brief_actual_contribution: Systematically analyzes conformal factuality filtering for RAG-based LLMs, introducing informativeness-aware metrics and showing fragility under distribution shifts/distractors, while comparing entailment vs LLM-based scorers for efficiency.

title: GRACE: Reinforcement Learning for Grounded Response and Abstention under Contextual Evidence
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes GRACE, an RL framework with multi-stage gated rewards that trains RAG models to ground answers in cited evidence or explicitly abstain when retrieved context is insufficient.

title: Exploring Knowledge Conflicts for Faithful LLM Reasoning: Benchmark and Method
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes ConflictQA, a benchmark for cross-source knowledge conflicts (text vs. KG) in RAG, evaluates 12 LLMs, and introduces XoT, a two-stage explanation-based prompting method to improve faithful reasoning under conflicts.

title: ERA: Evidence-based Reliability Alignment for Honest Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes ERA, an evidential deep learning framework using Dirichlet distributions and Dempster-Shafer theory to disentangle epistemic/aleatoric uncertainty and quantify knowledge conflicts between parametric memory and retrieved context, enabling calibrated abstention in RAG.

title: Cordon-MAS: Defending RAG against Knowledge Poisoning via Information-Flow Control
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces CORDON-MAS, a multi-agent defense framework that enforces information-flow separation between untrusted retrieved evidence and the final synthesizer to defend RAG against knowledge poisoning, reducing ASR by 92.4% across five BEIR datasets.

title: Beyond Explicit Refusals: Soft-Failure Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Formalizes 'soft failure' as a stealthy availability threat to RAG and introduces DEJA, an evolutionary black-box framework that crafts adversarial documents inducing fluent but non-informative answers while evading perplexity-based defenses.

title: Architecture Matters: Comparing RAG Systems under Knowledge Base Poisoning
brief_actual_contribution: Benchmarks four RAG architectures (vanilla, agentic, MADAM-RAG, RLM) under N=1 knowledge base poisoning attacks (naive and CorruptRAG-AK) on Natural Questions, showing a ~58pp ASR spread across architectures and introducing a behavioral taxonomy for evaluating contradiction handling.

title: ArbGraph: Conflict-Aware Evidence Arbitration for Reliable Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes ArbGraph, a pre-generation evidence arbitration framework that decomposes retrieved documents into atomic claims, builds a support/contradiction graph, and iteratively resolves conflicts to improve long-form RAG factuality and robustness to noise.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Paper's primary focus is knowledge conflict resolution rather than noisy retrieval/context compression per se, though it does address retrieval noise as part of its motivation.

title: Resisting Contextual Interference in RAG via Parametric-Knowledge Reinforcement
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Knowledgeable-R1, an RL framework with joint PK/CK/RPK sampling and adaptive advantage modulation to balance parametric vs. contextual knowledge use under conflicting or misleading retrieved context.

title: EcoSafeRAG: Efficient Security through Context Analysis in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes EcoSafeRAG, a defense framework that uses sentence-level segmentation and bait-guided contextual diversity clustering to detect and filter poisoned/adversarial documents in RAG without relying on LLM internal knowledge.

title: Disabling Self-Correction in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Stealthy Retriever Poisoning
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes DisarmRAG, a stealthy retriever-poisoning attack using contrastive-learning-based model editing and iterative prompt co-optimization to inject malicious instructions that bypass LLM self-correction in RAG systems.

title: CtrlRAG: Black-box Document Poisoning Attacks for Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes CtrlRAG, a black-box document poisoning attack against RAG using feedback-driven substitution localization and MLM-based perturbations, plus a knowledge-expansion defense.

title: Conflict-Aware Soft Prompting for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes CARE, which trains a context assessor to produce soft memory embeddings via grounded/adversarial soft prompting to mitigate context-memory conflicts in RAG without fine-tuning the base LLM.

title: Bounding Hallucinations: Information-Theoretic Guarantees for RAG Systems via Merlin-Arthur Protocols
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a Merlin-Arthur interactive proof training framework for RAG that induces abstention/reject behavior and information-theoretic mutual-information bounds (Explained Information Fraction) between context and answers, without requiring annotated unanswerable samples.

title: Beyond Black-Box Interventions: Latent Probing for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes ProbeRAG, which uses latent-space probing to detect aligned vs. conflicting knowledge, prunes noisy context, and applies conflict-aware attention fine-tuning to improve RAG faithfulness under knowledge conflicts.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Paper primarily targets knowledge conflict and faithfulness; noise filtering is one of three components.

title: Synchronous Faithfulness Monitoring for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces SynCheck, a lightweight synchronous monitor combining likelihood, uncertainty, context influence, and semantic alignment to detect unfaithful RAG outputs, and FOD, a faithfulness-oriented beam-search decoding algorithm, evaluated on a six-task long-form RAG faithfulness benchmark.

title: On the Vulnerability of Applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation within Knowledge-Intensive Application Domains
brief_actual_contribution: Demonstrates universal poisoning attacks against dense retrievers in RAG for medical/legal QA, explains via an orthogonal augmentation property, and proposes a Mahalanobis-distance detection defense.

title: Revisiting Robust RAG: Do We Still Need Complex Robust Training in the Era of Powerful LLMs?
brief_actual_contribution: Empirically shows that as LLM capacity grows, complex robust RAG training (sophisticated document selection, adversarial losses like RAAT/IRM) yields diminishing returns over simple training (e.g., random documents), attributing this to stronger models' inherent calibration, generalization, and attention patterns.

title: After Retrieval, Before Generation: Enhancing the Trustworthiness of Large Language Models in RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces TRD benchmark covering four RAG scenarios (consistent, internal-faithful, external-faithful, refuse-to-answer) and proposes BRIDGE, a soft-bias allocator with decision tree to dynamically resolve internal/external knowledge conflicts including refusal.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes SURE-RAG, an aggregation protocol that turns pair-level claim-evidence relation distributions into answer-level sufficiency labels (supported/refuted/insufficient) with a calibrated selective-answering score, evaluated on a controlled HotpotQA-RAG v3 benchmark with risk-coverage and ECE metrics.

title: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Medical Multi-Modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces M3Att, a query-agnostic knowledge poisoning attack on medical multimodal RAG that combines distribution-guided retrieval hijacking via PGD-perturbed images with clinical ambiguity-guided misinformation injection in paired texts.

title: BalanceRAG: Joint Risk Calibration for Cascaded Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes BalanceRAG, a training-free joint risk-calibration framework for cascaded LLM-only/RAG routing that uses sequential graphical testing over a threshold lattice to certify operating points with finite-sample selection-conditioned risk control, supporting abstention and multi-risk (retrieval-rate) constraints.

title: The Silent Saboteur: Imperceptible Adversarial Attacks against Black-Box Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes ReGENT, an RL-based black-box adversarial attack that applies imperceptible word substitutions to a target document so it enters top-k retrieval and manipulates RAG generation, demonstrating high attack success while preserving naturalness.

title: The RAG Paradox: A Black-Box Attack Exploiting Unintentional Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes PARADOX, a realistic black-box corpus poisoning attack on RAG systems that infers retriever preferences from exposed sources to craft natural-looking poisoned documents.

title: Who Taught the Lie? Responsibility Attribution for Poisoned Knowledge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes RAGOrigin, a black-box forensic/attribution framework that identifies poisoned texts in a RAG knowledge database responsible for misgeneration events, using adaptive scope selection and a combined retrieval/semantic/generation responsibility score.

title: Topic-FlipRAG: Topic-Orientated Adversarial Opinion Manipulation Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation Models
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces Topic-FlipRAG, a black-box topic-oriented adversarial attack that combines LLM knowledge-guided document edits with gradient-based ranking triggers to manipulate stance polarity in RAG outputs across related queries.

title: Resolving Conflicting Evidence in Automated Fact-Checking: A Study on Retrieval-Augmented LLMs
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces the CONFACT dataset and evaluates RAG-based LLMs on fact-checking with conflicting evidence from sources of varying credibility, proposing strategies that integrate media source credibility into retrieval/ranking/generation.

title: RAG-Pull: Turning Retrieval into a Code-Injection Channel via Invisible Unicode Perturbations
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces RAG-PULL, an imperceptible Unicode-perturbation attack on code-RAG pipelines that manipulates queries and/or corpus snippets to steer retrieval toward attacker-controlled vulnerable code, demonstrating transferability across 14 embedders.

title: Poisoned-MRAG: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks to Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Poisoned-MRAG, a knowledge poisoning attack on multimodal RAG that injects malicious image-text pairs to manipulate VLM outputs, with both dirty-label and clean-label variants and evaluation of defenses.

title: One Pic is All it Takes: Poisoning Visual Document Retrieval Augmented Generation with a Single Image
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes targeted and universal poisoning attacks on visual document RAG systems by injecting a single adversarial image into the KB, using multi-objective PGD optimization, evaluated across white-box and black-box settings and defenses.

title: FlippedRAG: Black-Box Opinion Manipulation Adversarial Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes FlippedRAG, a black-box transfer attack that imitates the RAG retriever to craft poisoning triggers shifting RAG-generated opinions on controversial topics, and evaluates defenses.

title: Faithfulness-Aware Uncertainty Quantification for Fact-Checking the Output of Retrieval Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes FRANQ, a faithfulness-aware uncertainty quantification method for RAG outputs with calibration, and introduces a long-form QA dataset annotated for factuality and faithfulness.

title: Defending against Indirect Prompt Injection by Instruction Detection
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a detection-based defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG/LLM systems using hidden states and gradients from intermediate layers as discriminative features.

title: DeRAG: Black-box Adversarial Attacks on Multiple Retrieval-Augmented Generation Applications via Prompt Injection
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes DeRAG, a gradient-free black-box adversarial attack that uses Differential Evolution to craft short adversarial suffixes that re-rank a target (incorrect) document into top-k retrieval results in RAG pipelines, degrading downstream answer quality.

title: ConfRAG: Confidence-Guided Retrieval-Augmenting Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes ConfQA fine-tuning to teach LLMs to abstain on low-confidence factual questions, and ConfRAG which uses these abstentions as a trigger for invoking retrieval, reducing hallucinations and unnecessary retrievals.

title: Chain-of-Thought Poisoning Attacks against R1-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a knowledge-base poisoning attack that wraps fake knowledge in chain-of-thought reasoning templates to mislead R1-based RAG systems, improving attack success over PoisonedRAG and prompt-hijacking baselines.

title: Who's Who: Large Language Models Meet Knowledge Conflicts in Practice
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces WhoQA, a 5K-question benchmark that induces natural knowledge conflicts by asking about shared properties of same-name Wikipedia entities, and shows LLMs degrade and often bias toward popular answers under such conflicts.

title: Unanswerability Evaluation for Retrieval Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces UAEval4RAG, a framework with a six-category taxonomy of unanswerable requests and an automated pipeline to synthesize them for arbitrary knowledge bases, evaluating RAG systems' abstention/rejection ability via unanswered and acceptable ratios.

title: Studying Large Language Model Behaviors Under Context-Memory Conflicts With Real Documents
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a realistic framework for studying context-memory knowledge conflicts using real factual documents that contradict the model's incorrect parametric answers, finding that LLMs usually update but exhibit a 'parametric bias' where an incorrect parametric answer appearing in context increases update failure.

title: RetrievalQA: Assessing Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Short-form Open-Domain Question Answering
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces RetrievalQA, a 1,271-question benchmark covering new-world and long-tail knowledge to evaluate adaptive RAG methods, and proposes TA-ARE, an ICL-based calibration-free adaptive retrieval method.

title: Rag and Roll: An End-to-End Evaluation of Indirect Prompt Manipulations in LLM-based Application Frameworks
brief_actual_contribution: Presents Rag-n-Roll, an end-to-end evaluation framework testing indirect prompt injection / corpus poisoning attacks against various RAG configurations, finding existing ranking-focused attacks plateau around 40% success.

title: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG
brief_actual_contribution: RAFT is a fine-tuning recipe for domain-specific RAG that trains LLMs with a mix of golden and distractor documents and chain-of-thought answers quoting source spans, improving robustness to irrelevant retrieved context.
issues: citation/grounding paragraph: RAFT does train models to quote source spans verbatim, so the claim partially matches; however RAFT is not really a 'grounding method' for claim-level citation verification but a domain-specific RAG fine-tuning recipe.

title: Poisoned LangChain: Jailbreak LLMs by LangChain
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces Poisoned-LangChain, an indirect jailbreak attack on LLMs via RAG by injecting disguised malicious content into the external knowledge base, triggered by keywords, achieving high attack success rates on six Chinese LLMs.

title: Neural Exec: Learning (and Learning from) Execution Triggers for Prompt Injection Attacks
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes optimization-based generation of prompt-injection execution triggers (Neural Exec) that persist through RAG preprocessing pipelines, achieving high attack success rates against open-source LLMs.

title: Cutting Off the Head Ends the Conflict: A Mechanism for Interpreting and Mitigating Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Identifies memory heads and context heads in later transformer layers as the pivotal point where knowledge conflicts emerge, and proposes PH3 (pruning heads via path patching) to flexibly steer LMs toward internal memory or external context.

title: Backdoored Retrievers for Prompt Injection Attacks on Retrieval Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Investigates prompt injection attacks against RAG via corpus poisoning and backdoored dense retrievers, demonstrating high attack success rates for malicious link insertion, advertising, and denial-of-service objectives across multiple LLMs.

title: Tricking Retrievers with Influential Tokens: An Efficient Black-Box Corpus Poisoning Attack
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes DIGA, a black-box genetic-algorithm corpus poisoning attack that exploits retrievers' token-order insensitivity and bias towards influential tokens to craft adversarial passages efficiently.

title: Token-Level Precise Attack on RAG: Searching for the Best Alternatives to Mislead Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces TPARAG, a token-level adversarial attack framework that uses a lightweight white-box LLM to craft malicious passages targeting both retrieval and generation in RAG systems under black- and white-box settings.

title: RIPRAG: Hack a Black-box Retrieval-Augmented Generation Question-Answering System with Reinforcement Learning
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces RIPRAG, an RL-based black-box poisoning attack against RAG QA systems, using black-box feedback (RLBF) and a novel BRPO algorithm to generate adversarial documents that achieve high attack success rates even against defended systems.

title: RAG Safety: Exploring Knowledge Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a black-box data poisoning attack on KG-based RAG systems that injects perturbation triples to complete misleading inference chains, demonstrating substantial QA degradation across four KG-RAG methods on WebQSP and CWQ.

title: One shot dominance: Knowledge poisoning attack on retrieval-augmented generation systems
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces AuthChain, a knowledge poisoning attack that injects a single authoritative, evidence-chain-structured poisoned document into a RAG knowledge base to manipulate LLM outputs even for multi-hop queries, evading existing RAG defenses.

title: MM-PoisonRAG: Disrupting Multimodal RAG with Local and Global Poisoning Attacks
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces MM-PoisonRAG, a framework with localized and globalized poisoning attacks on multimodal RAG showing high attack success and ineffective defenses.

title: Hoist with His Own Petard: Inducing Guardrails to Facilitate Denial-of-Service Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLMs
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces MutedRAG, a denial-of-service attack on RAG that injects minimal jailbreak prompts into the corpus to weaponize LLM safety guardrails into refusing legitimate queries.

title: A Few Words Can Distort Graphs: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces two knowledge poisoning attacks (targeted TKPA and universal UKPA) against GraphRAG that modify a tiny fraction of source text to distort the constructed knowledge graph and evade existing defenses.

title: Traceback of Poisoned Texts in Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes RAGForensics, a post-hoc traceback system that identifies poisoned texts in a RAG knowledge database from user feedback on incorrect outputs, evaluated against PoisonedRAG and instruction injection attacks.

title: RevPRAG: Revealing Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation through LLM Activation Analysis
brief_actual_contribution: RevPRAG detects RAG poisoning attacks by analyzing distinct activation patterns of LLMs when generating correct vs. poisoned responses, achieving ~98% TPR and ~1% FPR across multiple LLMs and retrievers.

title: Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes an evaluation framework and instruction-based methods for detecting and resolving knowledge conflicts between LLM parametric knowledge and contextual information, across three tasks of increasing difficulty.

title: Beyond RAG vs. Long-Context: Learning Distraction-Aware Retrieval for Efficient Knowledge Grounding
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes LDAR, a lightweight learned retriever that selects passages from a similarity quantile band to balance information coverage and distraction, outperforming RAG and long-context approaches with lower token usage.

title: Whose Facts Win? LLM Source Preferences under Knowledge Conflicts
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a synthetic-source, synthetic-conflict evaluation framework to measure LLM source preferences under inter-context knowledge conflicts across 13 open models, finds a consistent credibility hierarchy that can be flipped by repetition, and proposes a fine-tuning method to mitigate repetition bias.

title: Towards Unsupervised Adversarial Document Detection in Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
brief_actual_contribution: A preliminary unsupervised method to detect adversarial documents in RAG by treating generator activations, output embeddings, and TokenSAR entropy as outlier indicators via Grubbs' test.

title: Towards Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Review of Threats, Defenses and Benchmarks
brief_actual_contribution: A comprehensive survey of RAG security threats (poisoning, MIA, adversarial, embedding inversion, indirect injection), defenses (encryption, DP, federated learning, sanitization), and evaluation benchmarks.

title: Towards Dependable Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Factual Confidence Prediction
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a two-stage RAG dependability pipeline: conformal prediction for retrieval chunk filtering with statistical guarantees, plus an attention-based (lookback ratio) classifier for hallucination/factuality detection.

title: The Curse of Helpfulness: Inverse Scaling Law in Robustness to Distractor Instructions via DistractionIF
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes DistractionIF, a benchmark measuring LLM robustness to benign instruction-like noise embedded in reference text, reveals an inverse scaling phenomenon, and shows GRPO can restore robustness.

title: RefineRAG: Word-Level Poisoning Attacks via Retriever-Guided Text Refinement
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces RefineRAG, a two-stage poisoning attack on RAG that combines macro seed generation with retriever-guided word-level MLM refinement, achieving high ASR with low perplexity and strong transferability.

title: RedVisor: Reasoning-Aware Prompt Injection Defense via Zero-Copy KV Cache Reuse
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes RedVisor, a two-phase prompt injection defense using a top-layer gated adapter for explainable injection detection followed by guided generation, with zero-copy KV cache reuse for efficient deployment.

title: PIDP-Attack: Combining Prompt Injection with Database Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes PIDP-Attack, a compound RAG attack combining query-time prompt injection with corpus poisoning that misleads LLMs without prior knowledge of user queries.

title: Neuro-RIT: Neuron-Guided Instruction Tuning for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Language Model
brief_actual_contribution: Neuro-RIT identifies relevant vs. irrelevant context-aware neurons via attribution and applies two-stage instruction tuning to suppress noise-aware neurons while reinforcing evidence distillation, improving RALM robustness to noisy retrieval.

title: MTRAG-UN: A Benchmark for Open Challenges in Multi-Turn RAG Conversations
brief_actual_contribution: MTRAG-UN is a 666-task multi-turn RAG benchmark spanning 6 domains, focusing on unanswerable, underspecified, non-standalone questions and clarification responses, with retrieval and generation evaluations showing frontier LLMs struggle with these cases.

title: MPIB: A Benchmark for Medical Prompt Injection Attacks and Clinical Safety in LLMs
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces MPIB, a benchmark of 9,697 instances for evaluating direct and RAG-mediated prompt injection attacks on LLMs in clinical settings, with a clinical harm taxonomy and outcome-based CHER metric alongside ASR.

title: Lost in the Evidence? Reproducing Document Position and Context Size Effects in RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Reproducibility study of positional bias (lost-in-the-middle) and context size effects in RAG, introducing a topic-budget calibration procedure and analyzing interactions among retrieval quality, ordering, context size, and model scale.

title: LogicPoison: Logical Attacks on Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes LogicPoison, a topology-targeted attack on GraphRAG that uses type-preserving entity swapping to corrupt knowledge graph logical reasoning chains while evading content-based defenses.

title: KEPo: Knowledge Evolution Poison on Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces KEPo, a knowledge-evolution-based poisoning attack against graph-based RAG that forges evolution paths to inject malicious facts into the KG, achieving SOTA attack success rates.

title: INTRYGUE: Induction-Aware Entropy Gating for Reliable RAG Uncertainty Estimation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes INTRYGUE, an induction-head-aware gating of predictive entropy for uncertainty quantification in RAG, addressing entropy-neuron-induced false uncertainty.

title: How Large Language Models Balance Internal Knowledge with User and Document Assertions
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a three-source (parametric/user/document) interaction evaluation framework and benchmarks 27 LLMs, revealing document-preference bias and limited discrimination of helpful vs. harmful external context, with SFT-based mitigation.

title: Hidden-in-Plain-Text: A Benchmark for Social-Web Indirect Prompt Injection in RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes OpenRAG-Soc, a benchmark and harness for evaluating indirect prompt injection and retrieval poisoning attacks on web-facing RAG systems, with deployable defenses (sanitization, normalization, attribution-gated prompting).

title: Hidden in the Metadata: Stealth Poisoning Attacks on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces MM-MEPA, a metadata-only poisoning attack on multimodal RAG that modifies textual metadata via constrained optimization to manipulate retrieval and generation while evading consistency-check defenses.

title: Grounded Decoding: Retrieval-Anchored Probability Fusion for Faithful RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces Grounded Decoding, a training-free decoding-time method that fuses full-RAG and retrieval-only next-token distributions via a KL-barycenter objective with adaptive weighting based on distributional conflict and retriever trust, improving factuality and citation quality.

title: Generating Leakage-Free Benchmarks for Robust RAG Evaluation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes SeedRG, a pipeline that regenerates multi-hop RAG benchmarks via reasoning-graph extraction and type-constrained entity replacement to reduce knowledge leakage and preserve reasoning difficulty, enabling more discriminative RAG evaluation.

title: Faithfulness-QA: A Counterfactual Entity Substitution Dataset for Training Context-Faithful RAG Models
brief_actual_contribution: Constructs a 99K-sample dataset by counterfactual NER-based entity substitution over SQuAD/TriviaQA to create controlled context-memory knowledge conflicts for training and evaluating context-faithful RAG models.

title: Decide Then Retrieve: A Training-Free Framework with Uncertainty-Guided Triggering and Dual-Path Retrieval
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes DTR, a training-free RAG framework that uses LLM generation uncertainty (negative log-likelihood) to decide whether to trigger retrieval, combined with a dual-path retrieval mechanism using both query and pseudo-context for adaptive evidence selection.

title: Can Small Language Models Use What They Retrieve? An Empirical Study of Retrieval Utilization Across Model Scale
brief_actual_contribution: Empirical study showing that sub-7B LMs fail to utilize retrieved context even under oracle retrieval, and that adding any context (including oracle) destroys parametric knowledge — a distraction effect that dominates over retrieval quality.

title: CODE: A Contradiction-Based Deliberation Extension Framework for Overthinking Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces CODE, a multi-agent knowledge-base poisoning attack on RAG systems that crafts contradiction-laden retrievable documents to inflate reasoning-token consumption of reasoning LLMs without degrading answer accuracy.

title: Bypassing Prompt Injection Detectors through Evasive Injections
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a GCG-based universal adversarial suffix that evades activation-based task-drift detectors for prompt injection, and a suffix-augmentation defense.

title: Benchmarking Knowledge-Extraction Attack and Defense on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a unified benchmark and design space for evaluating knowledge-extraction attacks and defenses on RAG systems across multiple datasets, retrievers, generators, and defense strategies.

title: Adversarial Hubness Detector: Detecting Hubness Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a multi-detector open-source scanner that uses robust statistics, cluster spread, stability, and domain/modality-aware analyses to detect adversarial hub poisoning in RAG vector databases.

title: Adaptive Stopping for Multi-Turn LLM Reasoning
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces MiCP, a conformal prediction framework for multi-turn LLM reasoning (adaptive RAG, ReAct) that allocates error budgets across turns to enable adaptive early stopping with coverage guarantees and an abstention option.

title: ALDEN: Boosting Private Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems via Active Learning and Distribution Estimation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes ALDEN, a black-box query-based attack on RAG systems that uses active learning (k-center) and decay-based topic distribution estimation to generate diverse malicious queries that extract more private chunks from the knowledge base than prior prompt-injection/extraction attacks.
issues: Adversarial corruption and security.: Paper is primarily a privacy/data-extraction attack rather than corpus poisoning, but fits the broader security/adversarial category.

title: A Sentence Relation-Based Approach to Sanitizing Malicious Instructions
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes SONAR, a sentence-level NLI-based sanitization defense that detects and prunes indirect prompt injection content from retrieved context in RAG/agent pipelines.

title: Your RAG is Unfair: Exposing Fairness Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Backdoor Attacks
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes BiasRAG, a two-phase backdoor attack on RAG that poisons the query encoder during pretraining and injects adversarial documents post-deployment to induce fairness-targeted biased outputs while preserving utility.

title: TruthfulRAG: Resolving Factual-level Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Knowledge Graphs
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes TruthfulRAG, a KG-based framework that extracts triples from retrieved content, performs query-aware graph retrieval, and uses entropy-based filtering to detect/resolve factual conflicts between parametric and external knowledge in RAG.

title: The Semantic Illusion: Certified Limits of Embedding-Based Hallucination Detection in RAG Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Applies split conformal prediction to RAG hallucination detection, showing that embedding/NLI-based detectors fail catastrophically (100% FPR at 95% recall) on real RLHF-aligned hallucinations while LLM judges succeed, demonstrating limits of semantic-similarity-based calibration.

title: The Hidden Threat in Plain Text: Attacking RAG Data Loaders
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces stealthy document-level poisoning attacks (invisible characters, hidden text, font tricks) targeting RAG data loaders, with a toolkit (PhantomText) demonstrating high ASR across loaders and end-to-end RAG systems.

title: Separate the Wheat from the Chaff: Winnowing Down Divergent Views in Retrieval Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes WinnowRAG, a training-free multi-agent RAG framework that clusters retrieved documents and uses a critic LLM to iteratively filter out noisy ones while retaining useful content.

title: Search Wisely: Mitigating Sub-optimal Agentic Searches By Reducing Uncertainty
brief_actual_contribution: Defines over-search and under-search in agentic RAG, links them to model uncertainty about knowledge boundaries, and proposes β-GRPO, a confidence-thresholded RL reward that improves agentic search decisions.

title: SciRerankBench: Benchmarking Rerankers Towards Scientific Retrieval-Augmented Generated LLMs
brief_actual_contribution: SciRerankBench is a scientific RAG benchmark with three context-perturbation tasks (noisy, semantically similar-but-irrelevant, counterfactual) to evaluate 13 rerankers across 11 LLMs.

title: SUGAR: Leveraging Contextual Confidence for Smarter Retrieval
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes SUGAR, which uses semantic entropy as an uncertainty signal to adaptively choose between no retrieval, single-step, or multi-step retrieval in open-domain QA.

title: RoseRAG: Robust Retrieval-augmented Generation with Small-scale LLMs via Margin-aware Preference Optimization
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes RoseRAG, a framework training small-scale LLMs with margin-aware preference optimization (rejection sampling + contrastive preference selection) to make RAG robust to noisy/irrelevant retrieved documents.

title: Robustness via Referencing: Defending against Prompt Injection Attacks by Referencing the Executed Instruction
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a prompt-engineering defense against direct and indirect prompt injection attacks that asks LLMs to tag each executed instruction with a reference, then filters out responses whose tags don't match the original input instruction.

title: RobustMask: Certified Robustness against Adversarial Neural Ranking Attack via Randomized Masking
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces RobustMask, a randomized-masking smoothing defense providing certified top-K robustness for neural ranking models against adversarial perturbations, with applications to RAG retrieval security.

title: Retrieval as a Decision: Training-Free Adaptive Gating for Efficient RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes TARG, a training-free single-shot gate that uses prefix-logit uncertainty signals (entropy, top-1/top-2 margin, small-N variance) to decide whether RAG retrieval is needed, calibrated via threshold/quantile to a retrieval budget.

title: Rethinking All Evidence: Enhancing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Conflict-Driven Summarization
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes CARE-RAG, a framework that elicits diverse parametric evidence, refines retrieved passages to remove noise, and uses a distilled LLaMA-3.2-3B conflict detector to summarize conflicts between internal and external knowledge before answering.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Primary focus is knowledge conflict resolution; noisy retrieval handling is a secondary aspect via context refinement.

title: Reasoning-Style Poisoning of LLM Agents via Stealthy Style Transfer: Process-Level Attacks and Runtime Monitoring in RSV Space
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces Reasoning-Style Poisoning of LLM agents via stealthy style transfer of retrieved documents, with a Reasoning Style Vector metric and a runtime monitor (RSP-M) that detects style-induced reasoning loops or premature convergence.
issues: Adversarial corruption and security: Paper also fits calibration_control via RSP-M runtime monitor, consistent with assigned categories.

title: RPO: Retrieval Preference Optimization for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Retrieval Preference Optimization (RPO), a DPO-variant alignment method that integrates retrieval-relevance reward into preference optimization, enabling LLMs to adaptively choose between parametric and retrieved knowledge under conflict.

title: RAGRank: Using PageRank to Counter Poisoning in CTI LLM Pipelines
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes RAGRank, a PageRank-derived source credibility score over document/citation graphs to defend RAG (especially CTI) systems against poisoning attacks, demonstrated on MS MARCO and CTI case studies.

title: Query-Level Uncertainty in Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a training-free query-level uncertainty estimator (Internal Confidence) using cross-layer/token self-evaluation probabilities, and applies it to adaptive RAG invocation and model cascading.

title: Quantifying and Improving the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Against Spurious Features in Grounding Data
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces SURE, a framework with taxonomy, data synthesis pipeline, and instance-level metrics for evaluating and mitigating RALM robustness against spurious (semantic-agnostic) features like format, style, and metadata in retrieved documents.

title: PrismRAG: Boosting RAG Factuality with Distractor Resilience and Strategized Reasoning
brief_actual_contribution: PrismRAG fine-tunes LLMs with synthetically generated distractor passages and strategized chain-of-thought reasoning to improve RAG factuality against semi-relevant retrieved noise.

title: Principled Context Engineering for RAG: Statistical Guarantees via Conformal Prediction
brief_actual_contribution: Applies split conformal prediction post-retrieval to filter retrieved snippets with finite-sample coverage guarantees, reducing context size 2-3x on NeuCLIR and RAGTIME without hurting factual accuracy.

title: Parallel Key-Value Cache Fusion for Position Invariant RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes KV-Fusion, a parallel key-value cache architecture that injects identical positional information across retrieved passages to make decoder-only RAG readers position-invariant and robust to irrelevant contexts.

title: PRGB Benchmark: A Robust Placeholder-Assisted Algorithm for Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: PRGB is a placeholder-based RAG benchmark evaluating LLM document utilization across multi-level noise filtering, combination, and reference reasoning, using placeholder substitution to disentangle parametric vs retrieved knowledge.

title: Noise-Robust Abstractive Compression in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces ACoRN, a noise-robust abstractive context compression method for RAG that uses offline data augmentation with irrelevant/factual-error documents and evidential-document-focused pseudo-label fine-tuning to improve ODQA performance.

title: NeuroGenPoisoning: Neuron-Guided Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLM via Genetic Optimization of External Knowledge
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a neuron-attribution + genetic-algorithm framework that crafts adversarial external passages activating 'Poison-Responsive Neurons' to override LLM parametric memory in RAG, achieving >90% population overwrite success across multiple LLMs and QA datasets.

title: Modeling Uncertainty Trends for Timely Retrieval in Dynamic RAG
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Entropy-Trend Constraint (ETC), a training-free dynamic RAG method that uses first- and second-order differences of token-level entropy plus dynamic smoothing to trigger timely retrieval, reducing delayed and redundant retrievals.

title: Micro-Act: Mitigating Knowledge Conflict in LLM-based RAG via Actionable Self-Reasoning
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes MICRO-ACT, a hierarchical action-space framework that decomposes knowledge into fine-grained comparisons to detect and resolve conflicts between retrieved evidence and LLM parametric knowledge in RAG QA.

title: MemoryGraft: Persistent Compromise of LLM Agents via Poisoned Experience Retrieval
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes MemoryGraft, a persistent memory poisoning attack against LLM agents (MetaGPT DataInterpreter) that injects malicious 'successful experiences' via benign-looking documentation, causing trigger-free behavioral drift through RAG retrieval.

title: Medusa: Cross-Modal Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Multimodal Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Medusa, a black-box cross-modal transferable adversarial attack on multimodal medical RAG systems that perturbs visual inputs to hijack retrieval and mislead generation.

title: LLMail-Inject: A Dataset from a Realistic Adaptive Prompt Injection Challenge
brief_actual_contribution: Presents the LLMail-Inject challenge and resulting dataset of adaptive indirect prompt injection attacks against an LLM-based email assistant, evaluating multiple defenses across LLMs and retrieval setups.

title: LLM-Independent Adaptive RAG: Let the Question Speak for Itself
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes 27 lightweight external features (entity popularity, question type/complexity, context relevance, etc.) for adaptive retrieval decisions, matching uncertainty-based methods at much lower compute.

title: Know Or Not: a library for evaluating out-of-knowledge base robustness
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces knowornot, an open-source library and leave-one-out methodology for evaluating LLM abstention/OOKB robustness in RAG, plus PolicyBench benchmark across four policy QA domains.

title: Investigating Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems on Unanswerable, Uncheatable, Realistic, Multi-hop Queries
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces CRUMQs, an automatic pipeline for creating difficulty-controlled, uncheatable, unanswerable multi-hop RAG benchmark queries, and evaluates leading RAG systems' abstention behavior.

title: ImportSnare: Directed "Code Manual" Hijacking in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces ImportSnare, a RAG poisoning attack on retrieval-augmented code generation that injects ranking and inducing sequences into documentation to make LLMs recommend malicious package dependencies.

title: How to make Medical AI Systems safer? Simulating Vulnerabilities, and Threats in Multimodal Medical RAG System
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces MedThreatRAG, a multimodal poisoning attack framework (textual, visual, cross-modal conflict injection) targeting medical RAG pipelines, evaluated on IU-Xray and MIMIC-CXR.

title: Exploring the Security Threats of Retriever Backdoors in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces VenomRACG, a stealthy and effective retriever backdoor attack for RACG that injects vulnerability-aware triggers, evades existing defenses, and induces LLMs to generate vulnerable code with <0.05% knowledge base poisoning.

title: Exploring the Security Threats of Knowledge Base Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Studies knowledge base poisoning attacks against retrieval-augmented code generation, showing that injecting vulnerable code examples causes LLMs to generate insecure code at high rates.

title: Energy Landscapes Enable Reliable Abstention in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Healthcare
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes an energy-based model trained over dense embeddings to enable reliable abstention in retrieval-augmented LLMs for women's health, outperforming softmax and kNN baselines on hard near-distribution OOD queries.
