title: EmoRAG: Evaluating RAG Robustness to Symbolic Perturbations
brief_actual_contribution: Demonstrates that injecting emoticons into queries and corpus documents can near-deterministically hijack RAG retrieval, evaluates the vulnerability across retrievers/generators/datasets, and proposes detection-based defenses.

title: END: Early Noise Dropping for Efficient and Effective Context Denoising
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes END, an early-layer linear probing method that detects and drops noisy chunks before full LLM forward pass, reducing distraction and computation in RAG/long-context QA.

title: Dynamic Context Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Mitigating Distractors and Positional Bias
brief_actual_contribution: Empirically analyzes distractor and positional ('lost in the middle') effects in RAG, and proposes a query-specific classifier predicting optimal k combined with LLM reranking to dynamically select context.

title: Do Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Adapt to Varying User Needs?
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces an evaluation framework (and synthetic URAQ dataset) testing RALMs under three user-need instructions crossed with context matching/conflict/irrelevance, showing model-family-dependent trade-offs between context faithfulness and memory reliance.

title: Defending Against Knowledge Poisoning Attacks During Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces a filtration phase between retrieval and generation that uses a statistical 'Freq-Density' property (and an ML classifier variant) to detect and remove adversarial passages injected via PoisonedRAG attacks.

title: Copy-Paste to Mitigate Large Language Model Hallucinations
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces Copy-Paste prompting and CopyPasteLLM (DPO-trained) that enforces high-copying from retrieved context to mitigate knowledge-conflict hallucinations, achieving large gains on FaithEval/ConFiQA counterfactual settings.

title: Confidence-Based Response Abstinence: Improving LLM Trustworthiness via Activation-Based Uncertainty Estimation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces an LSTM-based confidence model over LLM FFN activations for RAG to estimate response correctness and abstain when confidence is low, with Huber-loss calibration regularization, evaluated in a financial customer-support setting.

title: Bridging External and Parametric Knowledge: Mitigating Hallucination of LLMs with Shared-Private Semantic Synergy in Dual-Stream Knowledge
brief_actual_contribution: DSSP-RAG mitigates LLM hallucinations in RAG by combining unsupervised hallucination detection (sampling subspace stability), an Energy-Quotient-based external-knowledge noise filter, and a mixed-attention module that disentangles shared vs. private semantics between parametric and retrieved knowledge to resolve context-memory conflicts.
issues: Citation faithfulness / grounding: Paper is about decomposing external/parametric semantics to reduce hallucination, not about claim-level citation or quoting source spans. Fits the 'decompose external and parametric semantics' phrasing loosely but does not address citation verification. | Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression: Paper does include a noise-filtering component, so noisy_retrieval is acceptable. It also strongly fits knowledge_conflict (context-memory) and arguably calibration_control via hallucination detection threshold.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Knowledge Conflict for Large Multimodal Models
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces MMKC-Bench, a multimodal knowledge conflict benchmark for LMMs covering entity recognition, entity knowledge, and visual semantic conflicts in context-memory and inter-context settings, with analysis showing LMMs over-rely on parametric knowledge.

title: AttnTrace: Contextual Attribution of Prompt Injection and Knowledge Corruption
brief_actual_contribution: AttnTrace uses LLM attention weights (with top-K token averaging and context subsampling) to trace back malicious texts in long contexts that caused prompt-injection or knowledge-corruption attack outputs, outperforming prior traceback methods.

title: Accommodate Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-augmented LLMs: Towards Robust Response Generation in the Wild
brief_actual_contribution: Analyzes knowledge conflicts in RAG from an information-theoretic perspective and proposes Swin-VIB, a sliding-window variational information bottleneck method to adapt retrieved context and reduce LLM generation uncertainty under conflicts.

title: Supportiveness-based Knowledge Rewriting for Retrieval-augmented Language Modeling
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces SKR, a supportiveness-based knowledge rewriter that filters noisy/misleading retrieved content and compresses context, trained via DPO to optimize downstream LLM performance.

title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
brief_actual_contribution: SecAlign uses DPO-style preference optimization with secure vs insecure response pairs to defend LLMs against prompt injection attacks, reducing attack success rates below 10% even for optimization-based attacks.

title: REAR: A Relevance-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Open-Domain Question Answering
brief_actual_contribution: REAR augments an LLM-based RAG with an explicit relevance-assessment module and bi-granularity + noise-resistant training so the model adaptively weighs retrieved documents and resists irrelevant context.

title: Prompt Perturbation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a gradient-based prompt perturbation attack (GGPP) that adds short prefixes to user queries to steer RAG retrievers toward targeted wrong passages and trigger factual errors, plus probe-based detection defenses.

title: Parenting: Optimizing Knowledge Selection of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Parameter Decoupling and Tailored Tuning
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Parenting, a parameter-decoupling and tailored fine-tuning framework that localizes adherence vs. robustness subspaces in RALMs to balance reliance on external context and internal memory under knowledge conflict and noisy retrieval.

title: KnowPO: Knowledge-aware Preference Optimization for Controllable Knowledge Selection in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: KnowPO uses knowledge-aware DPO with constructed conflict/irrelevant context datasets to teach LLMs to adhere to relevant retrieved knowledge and ignore noise, mitigating contextual ignorance and overinclusion errors in RAG.

title: Investigating Context-Faithfulness in Large Language Models: The Roles of Memory Strength and Evidence Style
brief_actual_contribution: Investigates context-faithfulness of LLMs in knowledge-conflict scenarios, showing receptiveness to external evidence correlates negatively with internal memory strength and is influenced by evidence presentation style (e.g., paraphrasing).

title: Get my drift? Catching LLM Task Drift with Activation Deltas
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes detecting prompt injection / task drift in retrieval-augmented LLM apps by comparing activations before and after processing external data, training linear/metric probes that generalize to unseen attacks.

title: Entropy-Based Decoding for Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes a training-free entropy-based decoding method that ensembles document-parallel distributions weighted by low entropy and contrasts with a high-entropy parametric-knowledge layer, mitigating distraction from retrieved noise and knowledge conflict.

title: Enhancing Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with In-Context Learning
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes an in-context learning approach with MRC demonstrations (QA cases and conflict cases) to make RALMs more robust to unanswerable retrieved contexts and inter-context knowledge conflicts, without fine-tuning.

title: Dialectical Alignment: Resolving the Tension of 3H and Security Threats of LLMs
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes Dialectical Alignment using AI feedback to fine-tune LLMs so they dialectically resolve context-memory and inter-context conflicts, defending against poisoned RAG contexts while preserving in-context knowledge editing.

title: Defense Against Prompt Injection Attack by Leveraging Attack Techniques
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes training-free defenses against prompt injection attacks by repurposing attack techniques (ignore, escape, fake completion) as shield prompts, achieving low attack success rates on direct/indirect prompt injection benchmarks.

title: DYNAMICQA: Tracing Internal Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes DYNAMICQA, a benchmark of static, temporal, and disputable facts to study intra-memory knowledge conflicts in LMs and their interaction with retrieved context, along with a Coherent Persuasion score.

title: Blinded by Generated Contexts: How Language Models Merge Generated and Retrieved Contexts When Knowledge Conflicts?
brief_actual_contribution: Constructs context-conflicting datasets to study how LLMs merge generated vs. retrieved contexts, finding a bias toward generated contexts driven by similarity and semantic completeness.

title: Answerability in Retrieval-Augmented Open-Domain Question Answering
brief_actual_contribution: Investigates ODQA models' ability to abstain when retrieved excerpts are irrelevant; shows random-context training fails to generalize to semantically related but unanswerable contexts, and training with SQuAD 2.0 unanswerables enables near-perfect abstention.

title: Adaptive Contrastive Decoding in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Handling Noisy Contexts
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces Adaptive Contrastive Decoding, which uses entropy-based weighting to balance parametric vs. contextual knowledge during decoding, improving robustness in RAG with noisy retrieved contexts and handling knowledge conflicts.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
brief_actual_contribution: RECOMP introduces extractive and abstractive compressors that summarize retrieved documents (or return empty strings for selective augmentation) prior to prepending to a frozen LM, reducing tokens and mitigating irrelevant-context degradation.

title: Merging Generated and Retrieved Knowledge for Open-Domain QA
brief_actual_contribution: COMBO is a compatibility-oriented framework that pairs LLM-generated and retrieved passages via trained evidentiality/consistency discriminators to mitigate parametric–retrieval knowledge conflicts in open-domain QA.

title: QuCo-RAG: Quantifying Uncertainty from the Pre-training Corpus for Dynamic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces QuCo-RAG, a dynamic RAG framework that uses pre-training corpus statistics (entity frequency and co-occurrence via Infini-gram) instead of model-internal confidence to quantify uncertainty and adaptively trigger retrieval, improving multi-hop QA performance.

title: Spa-VLM: Stealthy Poisoning Attacks on RAG-based VLM
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces Spa-VLM, a stealthy data-poisoning attack against multimodal RAG-based vision-language models that injects crafted adversarial image-text pairs into the knowledge base to induce targeted misleading answers.

title: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Defenses, and Future Directions
brief_actual_contribution: A survey of RAG security organized via the SLOT taxonomy (Surface/Layer/Objective/Target), mapping attacks, defenses, and evaluation benchmarks along the knowledge-access pipeline.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
brief_actual_contribution: Self-RAG trains an LM to adaptively decide when to retrieve and to critique its own generations via special reflection tokens, improving factuality and citation accuracy.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces 'sufficient context' as a property of (query, context) pairs, builds an LLM autorater to label it, analyzes RAG hallucination/abstention behavior stratified by sufficiency, and proposes a selective generation method combining sufficiency with self-confidence to reduce hallucinations.
issues: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression: Primary contribution is answerability/calibration/abstention rather than distraction or compression per se.

title: TrojanRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Can Be Backdoor Driver in Large Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes TrojanRAG, a backdoor attack on the RAG retriever using contrastive learning and knowledge-graph-enhanced poisoned contexts to make triggered queries induce targeted, biased, or jailbreaking LLM outputs while keeping LLM weights untouched.

title: Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
brief_actual_contribution: Survey of trustworthiness in RAG across six dimensions (factuality, robustness, fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy) with a benchmark (TRC Bench) evaluating 19 LLMs.

title: Towards Trustworthy Retrieval Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
brief_actual_contribution: A comprehensive survey of trustworthy RAG systems organized around six pillars (reliability, privacy, safety, fairness, explainability, accountability), with taxonomies, evaluation protocols, and applications in healthcare, law, and education.
issues: Adversarial corruption and security.: This is a survey, not a primary adversarial-corruption work; it covers safety as one of many axes.

title: Tug-of-War Between Knowledge: Exploring and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
brief_actual_contribution: Proposes an evaluation framework for knowledge conflicts in RALMs (internal vs. external and among external evidence), reveals Dunning-Kruger-like and confirmation bias behaviors, and introduces Conflict-Disentangle Contrastive Decoding (CD2) to calibrate model confidence.

title: UncertaintyRAG: Span-Level Uncertainty Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval-Augmented Generation
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces UncertaintyRAG, which uses SNR-based span-level uncertainty from an LLM to score chunk-pair similarity, enabling unsupervised training of a lightweight retrieval model for long-context RAG that generalizes under distribution shift.
issues: Calibration: The paper uses span-level uncertainty primarily to train the retrieval model (construct positive/negative pairs via SNR-based similarity), not directly to improve robustness under distribution shift in generation. The claim 'improve retrieval training and robustness under distribution shift' is accurate to the paper.

title: When to Retrieve: Teaching LLMs to Utilize Information Retrieval Effectively
brief_actual_contribution: Introduces ADAPT-LLM, which fine-tunes an LLM to emit a special <RET> token to trigger external retrieval only when its parametric memory is insufficient, evaluated on PopQA.
